name: UI
comment:
**[Experimental]** An abstract class that represents an UI element. It wraps a [`Group`](#link) and supports UI event handling.
Extend this class to create custom UI elements.

signatures.comment: Create an UI element. You may also create a new UI using one of the static helper like [`UI.fromRectangle`](#link) or [`UI.fromCircle`](#link).

parameters.name: group
parameters.comment: a Group or an Iterable<PtLike> that defines the UI's appearance

parameters.name: shape
parameters.comment: specifies the shape of the Group

parameters.name: states
parameters.comment: optional a state object keep track of custom states for this UI

parameters.name: id
parameters.comment: optional id string

accessors.name: group
accessors.comment: A group of Pts that defines this UI's shape.

accessors.name: id
accessors.comment: An unique id of the UI.

accessors.name: shape
accessors.comment: A string that describes this UI's shape.

signatures.comment: Get a specific UI state. Unlike [`UI.state`](#link), this is a plain typed getter.

parameters.name: key
parameters.comment: state's name

signatures.comment: Continue to keep track of an actions even if it's not within this UI. Useful for hover-leave and drag-outside.

parameters.name: type
parameters.comment: a string defined in [`UIPointerActions`](#link)

signatures.comment: Listen for UI events and trigger action handlers.

parameters.name: type
parameters.comment: an action type. Can be one of UIPointerActions or a custom one.

parameters.name: p
parameters.comment: a point to check

parameters.name: evt
parameters.comment: a MouseEvent emitted by the browser (See [MDN docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MouseEvent))

parameters.name: type
parameters.comment: event type

parameters.name: which
parameters.comment: an ID number returned by [`UI.on`](#link). If this is not defined, all handlers in this type will be removed (built-in machinery like UIButton's click counting is unaffected). Note that after removal an id is stale — removing it twice may affect a handler that has since reused the slot.

signatures.comment: Add an event handler. Remember this UI will also need to be tracked for events, via `UI.track` or [`MultiTouchSpace.track`](#link).
signatures.returns_comment: an id number that reference to this handler, for use in [`UI.off`](#link), or -1 if nothing was registered

parameters.name: type
parameters.comment: event type, either one of [`UIPointerActions`](#link) or a custom type

parameters.name: fn
parameters.comment: a [`UIHandler`](#link) callback function: `fn( target:UI, pt:Pt, type:string, evt:MouseEvent )`

parameters.name: options
parameters.comment: optionally `{ once }` to remove the handler after its first call, and/or `{ signal }` with an [`AbortSignal`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AbortSignal) that removes it on abort (an already-aborted signal registers nothing)

signatures.comment: Take a custom render function to render this UI.

parameters.name: fn
parameters.comment: a render function

signatures.comment: Set a specific UI state. Unlike [`UI.state`](#link), this can also store `undefined`.

parameters.name: key
parameters.comment: state's name

parameters.name: value
parameters.comment: the value to set

signatures.comment: Get and/or set a specific UI state.
signatures.returns_comment: If `value` is changed, return this instance. Otherwise, return the value of the specific key.

parameters.name: key
parameters.comment: state's name

parameters.name: value
parameters.comment: optionally set a new value for this state.key

signatures.comment: Returns a string representation of this UI
Stop keeping track of this action

parameters.name: key
parameters.comment: an id returned by the [`UI.hold`](#link) function

Register a custom shape hit test, or override a built-in one. The shape
name can then be used when constructing a UI.

parameters.comment: a function `(group, pt, states) => boolean` that returns whether the point hits the shape
